## Barry fixtures

Repositories generated with Barry, and what a correct validator must conclude from each.

### M0

#### `m0-minimal-valid`: Minimal valid repository: TA, one CA, one ROA

The smallest repository that exercises a full chain: a trust anchor that
certifies one CA, which issues one ROA. Each publication point has the CRL
and manifest Barry generates. Nothing is overridden, so every object is
correct.

In M0 it proves the fixture pipeline works end to end: descriptor,
generation, metadata check, catalog and test helper. In later milestones
it is the positive baseline: every stage of the validator must accept it
and produce exactly one VRP. Invalid fixtures should differ from it in
one field, so a rejection can be traced to that one change.

- **Expected:** valid
- **RFC:** [6481 §2](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-2)), [8630 §2.2](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.2)), [6487 §4](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4)), [9286 §4](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4)), [9582 §4](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4))
- **Files:** [descriptor](../../test/fixtures/barry/m0-minimal-valid/case.repo) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/barry/m0-minimal-valid/case.exs) · [rsync tree](../../test/fixtures/barry/m0-minimal-valid/rsync)

### M1

#### `m1-cert-no-ski`: CA certificate without a Subject Key Identifier

The baseline tree with one change: the CA certificate has no Subject Key
Identifier extension. RFC 6487 section 4.8.2 says it MUST appear in all
resource certificates; it is also how children find their issuer (AKI),
so validation must reject the certificate.

In M1 it checks that a missing mandatory extension is not a decoding
error: the certificate decodes and simply has no SKI.

- **Expected:** invalid. A validator must reject:
  - `ta/ca1.cer`: no Subject Key Identifier; RFC 6487 section 4.8.2 requires it
- **RFC:** [6487 §4.8.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.2)), [6487 §4.8](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8)), [8897 §3.1](../rfc/rfc8897.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8897.html#section-3.1))
- **Files:** [descriptor](../../test/fixtures/barry/m1-cert-no-ski/case.repo) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/barry/m1-cert-no-ski/case.exs) · [rsync tree](../../test/fixtures/barry/m1-cert-no-ski/rsync)

#### `m1-cert-unknown-critical-extension`: CA certificate with an unrecognized critical extension

The baseline tree with one change: the CA certificate carries an extra,
critical extension with an OID no validator knows (1.3.6.1.4.1.99999.1).
RFC 6487 section 4.8 says a certificate-using system MUST reject a
certificate with a critical extension it does not recognize.

The extension is critical on purpose: for an unknown non-critical
extension the RFCs allow either ignoring or rejecting it (F-015 in
doc/rfc-findings.md), so that case is left for M4.

In M1 it checks that unknown extensions are kept, with their criticality,
instead of being dropped or failing the decode.

- **Expected:** invalid. A validator must reject:
  - `ta/ca1.cer`: unrecognized critical extension 1.3.6.1.4.1.99999.1; RFC 6487 section 4.8
- **RFC:** [6487 §4.8](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8)), [5280 §4.2](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-4.2))
- **Files:** [descriptor](../../test/fixtures/barry/m1-cert-unknown-critical-extension/case.repo) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/barry/m1-cert-unknown-critical-extension/case.exs) · [rsync tree](../../test/fixtures/barry/m1-cert-unknown-critical-extension/rsync)

#### `m1-cert-version-2`: CA certificate with X.509 version 2

The baseline tree with one change: the CA certificate's version field is
1, meaning X.509 v2. RFC 6487 section 4.1 requires version 3, and RFC 8897
section 3.1 requires relying parties to check the profile, so validation
must reject it.

In M1 it checks that decoding is structural: the certificate must still
decode, with version 2 visible, so that M4 can reject it with a precise
reason instead of a generic decode error.

- **Expected:** invalid. A validator must reject:
  - `ta/ca1.cer`: version is 2; RFC 6487 section 4.1 requires version 3
- **RFC:** [6487 §4.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.1)), [8897 §3.1](../rfc/rfc8897.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8897.html#section-3.1)), [5280 §4.1.2.1](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-4.1.2.1))
- **Files:** [descriptor](../../test/fixtures/barry/m1-cert-version-2/case.repo) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/barry/m1-cert-version-2/case.exs) · [rsync tree](../../test/fixtures/barry/m1-cert-version-2/rsync)

#### `m1-roa-prefixes`: ROA with IPv4 and IPv6 prefixes, with and without maxLength

A valid ROA for AS64496 with three prefixes: 1.1.0.0/17 with maxLength
24, 1.1.128.0/24 without maxLength, and 0101::/16 with maxLength 48. All
lie inside the EE certificate's resources and are in canonical order.

It checks that ROA decoding handles both address families, keeps an
absent maxLength distinct from a present one, and turns each address
into the right VRP: the maximum length is the prefix length when
maxLength is absent. M7 reuses it as a positive case producing exactly
these three VRPs.

- **Expected:** valid
- **RFC:** [9582 §4.3](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3)), [9582 §4.3.2.1](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.2.1)), [9582 §4.3.2.2](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.2.2)), [9582 §4.3.3](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.3))
- **Files:** [descriptor](../../test/fixtures/barry/m1-roa-prefixes/case.repo) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/barry/m1-roa-prefixes/case.exs) · [rsync tree](../../test/fixtures/barry/m1-roa-prefixes/rsync)

#### `m1-roa-version-2`: ROA with version 2

The baseline tree with one change: the ROA's version is 2. RFC 9582
section 4.1 says it MUST be 0, so validation must reject the ROA. This is
the incorrect repository from Barry's own tutorial.

In M1 it checks that the decoder doesn't treat the wrong version as a
decoding error: the ROA decodes with version 2 visible, and the version
is explicitly encoded (it isn't the DEFAULT), so the object is still DER.

- **Expected:** invalid. A validator must reject:
  - `ca1/roa1.roa`: version is 2; RFC 9582 section 4.1 requires 0
- **RFC:** [9582 §4.1](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.1))
- **Files:** [descriptor](../../test/fixtures/barry/m1-roa-version-2/case.repo) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/barry/m1-roa-version-2/case.exs) · [rsync tree](../../test/fixtures/barry/m1-roa-version-2/rsync)

Grouped by test module. Doctests are not listed: they are documented by the function docs they come from.

### `Lumina.FixturesMetadataTest`

[test/fixtures_metadata_test.exs](../../test/fixtures_metadata_test.exs)

Enforces that every Barry fixture documents why it exists, which RFC
sections it checks and what a validator must conclude from it, and that
its generated output is present. See doc/testing.md.

- every fixture has complete metadata and generated output

### `Lumina.ASN1Test`

[test/lumina/asn1_test.exs](../../test/lumina/asn1_test.exs)

Tests the wrapper around the ASN.1 modules compiled from the RFCs. Every
RPKI object is decoded through it, so it must decode real objects
faithfully, reject trailing data that asn1ct would silently ignore, and
never raise on malformed input, which a validator receives from
untrusted repositories.

- *real objects:* decodes the TA certificate and re-encodes it to identical bytes (RFC [5280 §4.1](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-4.1)), [5280 §A.1](../rfc/rfc5280.txt))
- *real objects:* decodes and re-encodes a CRL (RFC [5280 §5.1](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-5.1)), [5280 §A.1](../rfc/rfc5280.txt))
- *real objects:* decodes the ROA and manifest contents through the CMS envelope (RFC [5652 §12.1](../rfc/rfc5652.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5652.html#section-12.1)), [9582 §4](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4)), [9286 §A](../rfc/rfc9286.txt))
  A smoke test across modules; CMS, ROA and manifest decoding proper are #29-#31.
- *malformed input:* rejects trailing bytes after a valid value
  asn1ct decodes the value and silently drops anything after it. A
  validator must not accept an object with appended data, so the
  wrapper compiles with :undec_rest and rejects any leftover.
- *malformed input:* rejects empty, truncated and garbage input with an error, not an exception
- *malformed input:* never raises on random bytes
  Seeded, so the 2000 inputs are the same on every run.
- *malformed input:* a ROA with an address family other than IPv4 or IPv6 is an error, not a crash (RFC [9582 §4](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4)), [9582 §4.3.1](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.1)))
  RFC 9582's module limits addressFamily to IPv4 and IPv6 with an
  information object set, so the generated decoder exits on any other
  AFI (F-012 in doc/rfc-findings.md). The wrapper must turn that exit
  into an error.
- *malformed input:* reports an unknown module, an unknown type and non-binary input
- *malformed input:* encoding an invalid value returns an error
- every module key names a loaded, compiled ASN.1 module

### `Lumina.CertificateTest`

[test/lumina/certificate_test.exs](../../test/lumina/certificate_test.exs)

Tests decoding of RPKI resource certificates (RFC 5280 profiled by RFC
6487). Every later check (chain building, signatures, resources, URIs)
reads these structs, so decoding must expose every field faithfully, keep
the exact signed bytes, and stay structural: profile violations decode,
and only non-DER or unparseable input fails.

- *the m0-minimal-valid certificates:* the TA certificate is a self-issued v3 CA certificate valid 2026-2036 (RFC [6487 §4.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.1)), [6487 §4.4](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.4)), [6487 §4.5](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.5)), [6487 §4.6](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.6)), [6487 §4.8.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.1)), [6487 §4.8.4](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.4)))
- *the m0-minimal-valid certificates:* the Subject Key Identifier is the SHA-1 of the public key bits (RFC [6487 §4.8.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.2)), [5280 §4.2.1.2](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-4.2.1.2)))
  The key identifier is the SHA-1 of the subjectPublicKey bit string's value.
- *the m0-minimal-valid certificates:* the CA certificate points to the TA: AKI equals the TA's SKI and the issuer is the TA's subject (RFC [6487 §4.8.3](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.3)), [6487 §4.4](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.4)))
- *the m0-minimal-valid certificates:* the CA certificate's CRL, issuer, repository and manifest URIs and policy (RFC [6487 §4.8.6](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.6)), [6487 §4.8.7](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.7)), [6487 §4.8.8.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.8.1)), [6487 §4.8.9](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.9)))
- *the m0-minimal-valid certificates:* resources are decoded through Lumina.Resources (RFC [6487 §4.8.10](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.10)), [6487 §4.8.11](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.11)))
- *the m0-minimal-valid certificates:* the ROA's EE certificate (RFC [6487 §4.8.4](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.4)), [6487 §4.8.8.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.8.2)), [6488 §2.1.4](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.4)))
  An EE certificate has no Basic Constraints, signs objects, and its SIA points to the signed object.
- *the m0-minimal-valid certificates:* tbs_der is the exact tbsCertificate bytes from the input (RFC [5280 §4.1.1.1](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-4.1.1.1)))
  Signatures are over the exact DER of tbsCertificate, so it must be the input's bytes.
- *profile violations still decode (fixtures):* a version 2 certificate decodes with version 2 (RFC [6487 §4.1](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.1)))
- *profile violations still decode (fixtures):* a certificate without a Subject Key Identifier decodes without one (RFC [6487 §4.8.2](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8.2)))
- *profile violations still decode (fixtures):* an unrecognized critical extension is kept, with its OID and criticality (RFC [6487 §4.8](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4.8)))
- *malformed content:* a known extension whose value doesn't decode is marked malformed
  A broken known extension is reported in place, so validation can name it, not the whole certificate.
- *malformed content:* a validity time that isn't a real date is an error (RFC [5280 §4.1.2.5.1](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-4.1.2.5.1)))
- *malformed content:* non-DER, truncated and non-certificate input are errors naming the layer (RFC [6487 §4](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4)), [6481 §2.2](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-2.2)))

### `Lumina.CRLTest`

[test/lumina/crl_test.exs](../../test/lumina/crl_test.exs)

Tests decoding of CRLs (RFC 5280 §5, profiled by RFC 6487 §5). Revocation
checks and the CRL validation in M4 read these structs, so decoding must
expose issuer, dates, CRL Number and revoked entries faithfully, keep the
exact signed bytes, and stay structural: profile violations decode.

- *the m0-minimal-valid CRLs:* decode as v2 CRLs valid 2026-2036 with no revoked certificates (RFC [6487 §5](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-5)), [5280 §5.1.2.1](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-5.1.2.1)), [5280 §5.1.2.4](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-5.1.2.4)), [5280 §5.1.2.5](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-5.1.2.5)))
- *the m0-minimal-valid CRLs:* each CRL names its issuing CA and carries that CA's key identifier (RFC [6487 §5](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-5)), [5280 §5.1.2.3](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-5.1.2.3)), [5280 §5.2.1](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-5.2.1)))
  A CRL is matched to its issuer by name and by AKI = the issuer's SKI.
- *the m0-minimal-valid CRLs:* tbs_der is the exact tbsCertList bytes from the input (RFC [5280 §5.1.1.3](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-5.1.1.3)))
  Signatures are over the exact DER of tbsCertList, so it must be the input's bytes.
- *revoked certificates:* revoked entries decode with serial, date and entry extensions (RFC [5280 §5.1.2.6](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-5.1.2.6)), [5280 §5.3.1](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-5.3.1)))
  Barry can't write revoked entries yet (revokedCertificates is on its
  README's list of unimplemented fields), so this CRL is Barry's,
  decoded, given two entries and re-encoded.
- *structural decoding:* a CRL without a version field is version 1 (RFC [5280 §5.1.2.1](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-5.1.2.1)))
- *structural decoding:* a CRL without nextUpdate decodes with next_update nil (RFC [6487 §5](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-5)), [5280 §5.1.2.5](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-5.1.2.5)))
  nextUpdate is OPTIONAL in the ASN.1; requiring it is the profile's job (M4).
- *structural decoding:* a CRL Number that doesn't decode is marked malformed, and number/1 is nil (RFC [5280 §5.2.3](../rfc/rfc5280.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html#section-5.2.3)), [9829 §3.1](../rfc/rfc9829.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9829.html#section-3.1)))
- *structural decoding:* non-DER, truncated and non-CRL input are errors naming the layer

### `Lumina.DERTest`

[test/lumina/der_test.exs](../../test/lumina/der_test.exs)

Tests strict DER checking. RPKI requires DER (RFC 6488 §3 (l), RFC 6481
§2.2), but OTP's decoders accept BER, so every DER rule is checked here:
for each one, a minimal hand-built violation must be rejected with the
right rule and X.690 clause, and its valid counterpart accepted. X.690
isn't in doc/rfc, so its clauses are cited in each test's doc tag.

- *length octets:* rejects indefinite length
  X.690 10.1: DER uses the definite form only.
- *length octets:* rejects the long form for a short length
  X.690 10.1: lengths below 128 must use the one-octet short form.
- *length octets:* rejects a long-form length with a leading zero octet
  X.690 10.1: minimum number of octets, so no leading zero length octet.
- *length octets:* rejects the reserved length octet
  X.690 8.1.3.5: the first length octet 0xFF is reserved.
- *length octets:* rejects truncated input at every layer
- *identifier octets:* rejects the high-tag-number form for a low tag number
  X.690 8.1.2.2: tag numbers 0-30 use the single-octet form.
- *identifier octets:* rejects a high tag number with a leading 0x80 octet
  X.690 8.1.2.4.2: the first subsequent tag octet must not be 0x80.
- *identifier octets:* rejects end-of-contents octets
  X.690 8.1.5: end-of-contents octets only close indefinite lengths, which DER forbids.
- *primitive and constructed forms:* rejects a constructed OCTET STRING
  X.690 10.2: BIT STRING, OCTET STRING and character strings must be primitive.
- *primitive and constructed forms:* rejects a primitive SEQUENCE
  X.690 8.9.1 and 8.11.1: SEQUENCE and SET encodings are constructed.
- *universal types:* BOOLEAN
  X.690 11.1: TRUE is 0xFF; X.690 8.2.1: exactly one contents octet.
- *universal types:* INTEGER
  X.690 8.3.1 and 8.3.2: at least one octet, minimal two's complement.
- *universal types:* BIT STRING
  X.690 8.6.2.2-8.6.2.3: unused-bits octet 0-7, and 0 when empty; X.690 11.2.1: unused bits are zero.
- *universal types:* NULL
  X.690 8.8.2: NULL has no contents.
- *universal types:* OBJECT IDENTIFIER
  X.690 8.19.2: subidentifiers are minimal (no leading 0x80) and the last one terminates.
- *universal types:* UTCTime
  X.690 11.8: UTCTime is YYMMDDHHMMSSZ, seconds present, Z, no offset.
- *universal types:* GeneralizedTime
  X.690 11.7: GeneralizedTime ends in Z with seconds; fractional seconds don't end in 0.
- *universal types:* SET OF must be sorted
  X.690 11.6: SET OF elements in ascending order of their encodings.
- *structure:* rejects trailing bytes after the encoding
  X.690 8.1.1: an encoding is one TLV. RFC 6481 §2.2 and RFC 6488 §3 don't
  say what follows it; Lumina rejects anything (F-010 in doc/rfc-findings.md).
- *structure:* checks inside constructed values of any class, and reports the inner offset
- never raises on random bytes or random mutations of a real object
  Seeded, so the inputs are the same every run. Repository content is
  untrusted, so the checker must return an error, never raise. This
  test found a crash on an empty BIT STRING.
- *fixtures:* every object in m0-minimal-valid is DER (RFC [6488 §3](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-3)), [6481 §2.2](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-2.2)))
- *fixtures:* certificates and CRLs re-encode to identical bytes (RFC [6488 §3](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-3)), [6481 §2.2](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-2.2)))
- *check_canonical/3:* rejects an encoded DEFAULT value that a TLV walk can't see (RFC [9286 §A](../rfc/rfc9286.txt))
  X.690 11.5: a component equal to its DEFAULT is not encoded. A manifest
  with an explicit `version [0] INTEGER 0` passes the TLV walk, since every
  TLV is well formed, but isn't DER. Only re-encoding catches it.
- *check_canonical/3:* passes on decoding errors from the ASN.1 layer

### `Lumina.Fixtures.M0MinimalValidTest`

[test/lumina/fixtures/m0_minimal_valid_test.exs](../../test/lumina/fixtures/m0_minimal_valid_test.exs)

Checks that the m0-minimal-valid fixture loads and contains the files Barry
should produce for a TA -> CA -> ROA tree. This proves the fixture
pipeline works end to end (descriptor, generation, metadata, test helper)
before any object is decoded. Decoding and validation start in M1.

- loads with its metadata
- the rsync tree contains exactly the expected objects, each non-empty and readable
- RPKI objects are DER: each file starts with a SEQUENCE tag
- the TAL's rsync URI points to the trust anchor certificate in the tree
- the TAL's public key is base64 that decodes to a DER SEQUENCE
- the RRDP files are present

### `Lumina.ManifestTest`

[test/lumina/manifest_test.exs](../../test/lumina/manifest_test.exs)

Tests decoding of manifests (RFC 9286). Publication point validation (M5)
compares each file against the manifest's hash and checks the manifest
number and times, so these must decode exactly. Decoding is structural:
an empty file list decodes, and its rejection is validation's job (#37).

- *the m0-minimal-valid manifests:* list exactly the other files in their publication points (RFC [9286 §4.2](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.2)), [9286 §4.2.1](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.2.1)), [6481 §2.2](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-2.2)))
  Each manifest lists every other file at its publication point; the manifest itself is not listed.
- *the m0-minimal-valid manifests:* each listed hash is the SHA-256 of the file (RFC [9286 §4.2.1](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.2.1)), [7935 §2](../rfc/rfc7935.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7935.html#section-2)))
  Decode sanity only: each listed hash equals the SHA-256 of the file. Checking it is M5.
- *the m0-minimal-valid manifests:* version, manifest number, times and hash algorithm (RFC [9286 §4.2.1](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.2.1)))
- *structural decoding:* an empty file list decodes to no files (RFC [9286 §A](../rfc/rfc9286.txt), [9286 §7](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-7)))
  The module allows SIZE (0..MAX). Verified erratum 7118 and §7 forbid an
  empty list, but rejecting it is M5's job (#37, F-001), so it must decode.
- *structural decoding:* a 20-octet manifest number decodes exactly (RFC [9286 §4.2.1](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.2.1)))
  Manifest numbers up to 20 octets MUST be processable.
- *structural decoding:* a non-zero version decodes with that version (RFC [9286 §4.2.1](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4.2.1)))
- *structural decoding:* an explicitly encoded default version is not DER (RFC [9286 §A](../rfc/rfc9286.txt))
  X.690 11.5: version [0] equal to its DEFAULT 0 must not be encoded; only re-encoding catches it.
- *structural decoding:* a time that isn't a real date is an error
- *errors:* a signed object that isn't a manifest
- *errors:* non-DER and unparseable eContent

### `Lumina.ObjectTest`

[test/lumina/object_test.exs](../../test/lumina/object_test.exs)

Tests the entry point that decodes any repository file by its extension.
Repository processing and `lumina --print` go through it, so every
registered extension must reach the right decoder, a signed object's
eContent type must agree with its extension, and failures must name the
layer that failed.

- every file in every fixture decodes as the type its extension names (RFC [6481 §2.2](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-2.2)), [6481 §7.2](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-7.2)))
- registered extensions map to their types; others are unknown (RFC [6481 §2.2](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-2.2)), [6493 §9.2](../rfc/rfc6493.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6493.html#section-9.2)), [9323 §9.3](../rfc/rfc9323.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9323.html#section-9.3)), [9691 §11.3](../rfc/rfc9691.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9691.html#section-11.3)))
- a signed object whose eContent type disagrees with its extension is rejected (RFC [6481 §2.2](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-2.2)), [6488 §2.1.3.1](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.3.1)))
  A manifest published under a .roa name must not be taken for a ROA.
- Ghostbusters, RSC and TAK objects decode their envelope only (RFC [6493 §9.2](../rfc/rfc6493.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6493.html#section-9.2)), [9323 §9.3](../rfc/rfc9323.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9323.html#section-9.3)), [9691 §11.3](../rfc/rfc9691.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9691.html#section-11.3)))
  Ghostbusters, RSC and TAK eContent is decoded in M9; until then the envelope is decoded and eContent kept raw.
- *errors name the layer:* DER
- *errors name the layer:* ASN.1
- *errors name the layer:* envelope
- *errors name the layer:* eContent
- *errors name the layer:* type and file

### `Lumina.ResourcesTest`

[test/lumina/resources_test.exs](../../test/lumina/resources_test.exs)

Tests decoding of the RFC 3779 IP address and AS identifier extensions,
which resource-inclusion checks (M4/M6) depend on. Test vectors come from
the RFC's own worked examples (§2.1, §2.2.3.8, §2.2.3.9, Appendices B
and C), corrected where a verified erratum says the RFC is wrong
(erratum 6792, F-002 in doc/rfc-findings.md). The canonical-form checks
report violations without rejecting, because rejection belongs to
validation.

- *RFC 3779 Appendix B:* the first example decodes to the prefixes and range the RFC lists, in canonical form (RFC [3779 §B](../rfc/rfc3779.txt), [3779 §2.2.3.6](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.2.3.6)))
- *RFC 3779 Appendix B:* the second example, as corrected by erratum 6792, decodes to the stated prefixes (RFC [3779 §B](../rfc/rfc3779.txt))
  The second example as corrected by verified erratum 6792: the IPv4
  prefix 172.16/12 is ac10, not b010 as printed, and the IPv6 prefix is
  /48, not /47 as annotated. The family with SAFI 2 (multicast) inherits.
- *RFC 3779 Appendix B:* the second example's bytes as printed decode to 176.16/12 (RFC [3779 §B](../rfc/rfc3779.txt))
  Why the erratum matters: the bytes as printed in the RFC encode 176.16/12, not 172.16/12.
- *RFC 3779 Appendix C:* the AS example decodes to AS135, AS3000-AS3999, AS5001 and inherited RDIs (RFC [3779 §C](../rfc/rfc3779.txt), [3779 §3.2.3.4](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-3.2.3.4)))
- *the worked encodings in RFC 3779 §2.1 and §2.2.3:* addresses and prefixes (RFC [3779 §2.1.1](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.1.1)))
- *the worked encodings in RFC 3779 §2.1 and §2.2.3:* the all-addresses prefix and significant trailing zeros (RFC [3779 §2.1.2](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.1.2)))
  0/0 is a BIT STRING with no bits (03 01 00), and trailing zero bits are significant.
- *the worked encodings in RFC 3779 §2.1 and §2.2.3:* ranges expand min with zeros and max with ones (RFC [3779 §2.1.2](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.1.2)), [3779 §2.2.3.9](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.2.3.9)))
  Range ends: unspecified min bits are 0, unspecified max bits are 1.
- *the worked encodings in RFC 3779 §2.1 and §2.2.3:* the §2.2.3.8 prefix 128/4 covers 128.0.0.0 to 143.255.255.255 (RFC [3779 §2.2.3.8](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.2.3.8)))
- *edge cases:* ::/0, a single IPv6 address and the IPv4 /32 maximum
- *edge cases:* a prefix longer than the address family is an error
- *edge cases:* an unknown AFI keeps its bit strings undecoded
- *edge cases:* a range maximum with no one bits is accepted (erratum 2537) (RFC [3779 §2.2.3.9](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.2.3.9)))
  Verified erratum 2537 deleted the rule that a range maximum must contain
  a one bit. A maximum like 0.0.0.255 encodes as 24 zero bits (03 04 00
  00 00 00) and must be accepted.
- *edge cases:* malformed DER is an error
- *canonical form (reported, not enforced):* reports unsorted, overlapping and contiguous blocks (RFC [3779 §2.2.3.6](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.2.3.6)))
- *canonical form (reported, not enforced):* reports ranges that should be prefixes, non-minimal ends and inverted ranges (RFC [3779 §2.2.3.7](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.2.3.7)), [3779 §2.2.3.9](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.2.3.9)))
- *canonical form (reported, not enforced):* reports address families out of order or duplicated (RFC [3779 §2.2.3.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.2.3.3)))
- *canonical form (reported, not enforced):* reports AS identifiers that are unsorted, overlapping, contiguous or badly formed ranges (RFC [3779 §3.2.3.4](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-3.2.3.4)), [3779 §3.2.3.8](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-3.2.3.8)))
  Equal range ends are reported per erratum 7653, held for document update.
- *Barry fixture:* the m0-minimal-valid certificates carry Barry's default resources (RFC [3779 §2.2.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-2.2.3)), [3779 §3.2.3](../rfc/rfc3779.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3779.html#section-3.2.3)))
  Barry's README: the TA holds everything, and the first CA gets 1/8, 0100::/8 and AS 0x01000000-0x01FFFFFF.

### `Lumina.ROATest`

[test/lumina/roa_test.exs](../../test/lumina/roa_test.exs)

Tests decoding of ROAs (RFC 9582). VRP output (M7) is built from these
structs, so the AS, prefixes and maxLength must decode exactly, from both
the RFC's own example (Appendix A, read from the RFC text) and Barry
objects. The RFC 9582 §4.3 encoding recommendations are reported by
issues/1, not enforced.

- *RFC 9582 Appendix A:* the example eContent decodes to AS65536 and 2001:db8::/32 (RFC [9582 §A](../rfc/rfc9582.txt))
- *RFC 9582 Appendix A:* the complete example object matches its stated size and digest, and decodes (RFC [9582 §A](../rfc/rfc9582.txt))
  The Base64 is read from the RFC text itself; the size and SHA-256 the RFC
  states prove the transcription is exact before anything is decoded.
- *Barry ROAs:* the m0-minimal-valid ROA authorizes AS1234 for its EE certificate's prefixes (RFC [9582 §4.2](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.2)), [9582 §4.3](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3)))
- *Barry ROAs:* IPv4 and IPv6 prefixes with and without maxLength (RFC [9582 §4.3.2.1](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.2.1)), [9582 §4.3.2.2](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.2.2)))
  An absent maxLength stays nil; the VRP then uses the prefix length.
- *Barry ROAs:* a ROA with version 2 decodes with version 2 (RFC [9582 §4.1](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.1)))
- *issues/1 (reported, not enforced):* maxLength below the prefix length, or equal to it, is reported (RFC [9582 §4.3.2.2](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.2.2)))
- *issues/1 (reported, not enforced):* maxLength above the address width is a decode error (RFC [9582 §4](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4)), [9582 §4.3.2.2](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.2.2)))
  The module bounds maxLength by the family's address width (INTEGER (0..ub),
  ub = 32 or 128 via the information object set), so a maxLength above it
  fails at decode time rather than in issues/1 (F-012).
- *issues/1 (reported, not enforced):* IPv4-mapped IPv6 prefixes and repeated address families (RFC [9582 §4.3.1](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.1)))
- *issues/1 (reported, not enforced):* elements out of canonical order, and duplicates (RFC [9582 §4.3.3](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.3)), [9582 §4.3.3.1](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.3.1)))
- *errors:* a signed object that isn't a ROA
- *errors:* non-DER and unparseable eContent
- *errors:* an address family other than IPv4 or IPv6 is a decode error (RFC [9582 §4.3.1](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4.3.1)))
  The module's information object set rejects other AFIs at decode time (F-012).

### `Lumina.SignedObjectTest`

[test/lumina/signed_object_test.exs](../../test/lumina/signed_object_test.exs)

Tests decoding of the CMS SignedData envelope shared by all RPKI signed
objects (RFC 6488, RFC 5652). Signature checks (M5) need the exact signed
attributes and the EE certificate, and the ROA and manifest decoders need
the eContent, so the envelope must expose all of them faithfully.
Profile violations decode; only non-DER or unparseable input fails.

- *the m0-minimal-valid signed objects:* decode into SignedData with one EE certificate and the eContent type named (RFC [6488 §2](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2)), [6488 §2.1](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1)), [6488 §2.1.1](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.1)), [6488 §2.1.3.1](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.3.1)), [6488 §2.1.4](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.4)))
- *the m0-minimal-valid signed objects:* the EE certificate is decoded from the object's bytes, and the signer ID is its SKI (RFC [6488 §2.1.4](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.4)), [6488 §2.1.6.2](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.6.2)))
  The EE certificate keeps the exact bytes from the object; the signer is named by its SKI.
- *the m0-minimal-valid signed objects:* the signed attributes decode: content type, message digest and signing time (RFC [6488 §2.1.6.4](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.6.4)), [6488 §2.1.6.4.1](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.6.4.1)), [6488 §2.1.6.4.2](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.6.4.2)), [6488 §2.1.6.4.3](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.6.4.3)), [9589 §4](../rfc/rfc9589.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9589.html#section-4)))
  Decode sanity only: content-type matches eContentType and message-digest is SHA-256 of eContent.
- *the m0-minimal-valid signed objects:* signed_attrs_der is the object's signedAttrs bytes, re-tagged as a SET OF (RFC [5652 §5.4](../rfc/rfc5652.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5652.html#section-5.4)), [6488 §2.1.6.4](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.6.4)))
  The signature covers the DER of signedAttrs as a SET OF (tag 0x31), not
  the [0] IMPLICIT form in the object. Checked structurally here; the
  signature itself is verified in M5.
- *the m0-minimal-valid signed objects:* the signer's algorithms and signature (RFC [6488 §2.1.6.3](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.6.3)), [6488 §2.1.6.5](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.6.5)), [6488 §2.1.6.6](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.6.6)), [7935 §2](../rfc/rfc7935.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7935.html#section-2)))
- *content types:* decode_econtent/1 decodes ROA and manifest eContent with their ASN.1 types (RFC [9582 §4](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4)), [9286 §4](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4)))
- *content types:* the content types not decoded until M9 are named but have no decoder
- *content types:* an unknown eContent type decodes the envelope and leaves eContent raw
  An unknown eContent type is not a decoding error; the envelope decodes and eContent stays raw.
- *structural decoding:* a forbidden signed attribute decodes and is named (RFC [6488 §2.1.6.4](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1.6.4)), [9589 §4](../rfc/rfc9589.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9589.html#section-4)))
  RFC 9589 removed binary-signing-time; it must still decode so M5 can name it.
- *structural decoding:* a ContentInfo that isn't SignedData is an error (RFC [6488 §2.1](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-2.1)), [5652 §5.1](../rfc/rfc5652.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5652.html#section-5.1)))
- *structural decoding:* an embedded certificate that doesn't decode is an error naming the certificate
- *structural decoding:* signed attributes out of DER order are rejected as not canonical (RFC [6488 §3](../rfc/rfc6488.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6488.html#section-3)))
  signedAttrs is an [0] IMPLICIT SET OF, so a schema-less DER walk can't
  see its order (X.690 11.6). Only re-encoding catches unsorted
  attributes, and the signature covers these exact bytes.
- *structural decoding:* non-DER, truncated and unrelated input are errors naming the layer

### `LuminaTest`

[test/lumina_test.exs](../../test/lumina_test.exs)

Smoke test for the application module: the project builds and reports
its version.

- version/0 matches the version in mix.exs

### `Mix.Lumina.ASN1.CompileTest`

[test/mix/lumina/asn1/compile_test.exs](../../test/mix/lumina/asn1/compile_test.exs)

Checks that the patched modules in asn1/build/ compile with OTP's asn1ct
using DER encoding rules, and that the published modules in asn1/rfc/
don't. The second part shows each patch is still needed: if a future OTP
accepts a published module, the test fails, so the patch can be dropped.

- every patched module compiles with asn1ct (DER) (RFC [5280 §A.1](../rfc/rfc5280.txt), [5280 §A.2](../rfc/rfc5280.txt), [5652 §12.1](../rfc/rfc5652.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5652.html#section-12.1)), [3779 §A](../rfc/rfc3779.txt), [9582 §4](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4)), [9286 §A](../rfc/rfc9286.txt))
- each published module that has a patch fails to compile as is
  Documents F-005, F-006 and F-007 in doc/rfc-findings.md as observed compiler behaviour.
- modules without a patch compile as published

### `Mix.Lumina.ASN1.PatchTest`

[test/mix/lumina/asn1/patch_test.exs](../../test/mix/lumina/asn1/patch_test.exs)

Tests the ASN.1 patch applier and the allowed-change check. Patches exist
only to get the RFC modules past OTP's asn1ct, so the check must refuse
any patch that could change how a type encodes, such as deleting a field
or adding a constraint, and the applier must refuse to patch text that
doesn't match exactly.

- *parse/1:* reads hunks with their start line and operations
- *parse/1:* rejects a malformed hunk header, text before the first hunk and an empty patch
- *apply_hunks/2:* applies a hunk at exactly the line it names
- *apply_hunks/2:* refuses a hunk whose text doesn't match at that line, even if it matches elsewhere
  Strictness is the point: a patch that drifted must fail, not land on the wrong lines.
- *apply_hunks/2:* applies several hunks in order and refuses overlapping ones
- *check_allowed/1:* accepts a patch that only does what its kind allows
- *check_allowed/1:* requires every hunk to state its kind and reason
- *check_allowed/1:* rejects unknown and mixed kinds
- *check_allowed/1:* refuses a patch that deletes a field (RFC [9286 §A](../rfc/rfc9286.txt))
  A field deletion disguised as a compatibility patch would change what decodes.
- *check_allowed/1:* refuses a patch that changes a constraint (RFC [9286 §A](../rfc/rfc9286.txt))
  Applying erratum 7118 here (SIZE 1..MAX) was explicitly decided against
  (#37): errata are enforced in validation, never by patching modules.
- *check_allowed/1:* attribute-certificate patches may only add the opaque placeholders
- every committed patch passes the allowed-change check

### `Mix.Lumina.ASN1Test`

[test/mix/lumina/asn1_test.exs](../../test/mix/lumina/asn1_test.exs)

Tests extraction of ASN.1 modules from RFC text. Every ASN.1 type Lumina
compiles comes from these files, so extraction must keep the module
exactly as the RFC defines it and drop only page furniture and
whitespace. Synthetic RFC text covers the edge cases; the real modules
are checked too.

- *extract/2:* returns the module from its header to END, without page furniture
- *extract/2:* doesn't mistake a mention of the module name for its header
  Prose and IMPORTS lines mention module names too; only a header followed by DEFINITIONS counts.
- *extract/2:* fails when the module isn't there
- *extract/2:* fails when the module has no END line
- *extract/2:* fails when the module is not in the section the spec names
  Catches a wrong entry in the module list, which would cite the wrong RFC section.
- *whitespace handling:* collapses each run of blank lines into one
- *whitespace handling:* strips the common indentation and trailing whitespace only
- every configured module extracts from its RFC with its header, BEGIN and END (RFC [5280 §A.1](../rfc/rfc5280.txt), [5280 §A.2](../rfc/rfc5280.txt), [5652 §12.1](../rfc/rfc5652.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5652.html#section-12.1)), [5652 §12.2](../rfc/rfc5652.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5652.html#section-12.2)), [3779 §A](../rfc/rfc3779.txt), [9582 §4](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4)), [9286 §A](../rfc/rfc9286.txt))

### `Mix.Lumina.CatalogTest`

[test/mix/lumina/catalog_test.exs](../../test/mix/lumina/catalog_test.exs)

Tests rendering of doc/tests/CATALOG.md: content, grouping, order, links
and determinism. The catalog is committed and checked in CI, so output
must not depend on input order.

- says so when there are no fixtures or unit tests
- marks the file as generated
- groups by milestone and sorts by id within a milestone
- an entry shows the rationale, expected outcome, RFC links and files
- a valid fixture says so
- links are relative to where the catalog is written
- *unit tests:* lists each test module with its moduledoc, file and tests, in file order
- *unit tests:* shows the describe block, RFC references and doc tag of a test
- *unit tests:* says so for a module with only doctests
- *unit tests:* leaves out helper modules that don't use ExUnit.Case
- rendering is deterministic regardless of input order

### `Mix.Lumina.FixturesTest`

[test/mix/lumina/fixtures_test.exs](../../test/mix/lumina/fixtures_test.exs)

Tests the fixture metadata check: every way a fixture can be incomplete
or wrong must be reported, and case.exs must be read as data without
running any code in it. Fixtures are built in temporary directories.

- a complete fixture passes
- a valid fixture with Barry overrides passes
- *required metadata:* a missing rationale fails
- *required metadata:* a blank rationale fails
- *required metadata:* a missing RFC reference fails
- *required metadata:* an empty RFC list fails
- *required metadata:* an invalid RFC reference fails
- *required metadata:* a missing expected outcome fails
- *required metadata:* a malformed expected outcome fails
- *required metadata:* a rejected object that isn't in the rsync tree fails
- *required metadata:* an id that doesn't match the folder fails
- *required metadata:* an id that doesn't start with the milestone fails
- *required metadata:* an unknown milestone fails
- *required metadata:* an unknown key fails
- *required metadata:* bad Barry options fail
- *case.exs is data, not code:* function calls are rejected without being run
- *case.exs is data, not code:* string interpolation is rejected
- *case.exs is data, not code:* metadata that is not a map is rejected
- *case.exs is data, not code:* unparseable metadata is rejected
- *files:* a missing case.exs fails
- *files:* a missing descriptor fails
- *files:* missing generated output fails and says how to fix it
- load_all/2 returns passing fixtures and every problem

### `Mix.Lumina.RFCTest`

[test/mix/lumina/rfc_test.exs](../../test/mix/lumina/rfc_test.exs)

Tests RFC reference parsing and the section index built from doc/rfc.
These decide whether a test or fixture's RFC citation is accepted, so a
bug here would let wrong citations through or reject correct ones.

- *parse/1:* accepts numbered sections, appendices and appendix subsections
- *parse/1:* rejects malformed references
- *parse/1:* rejects values that are not strings
- *load_library/1:* loads every RFC in doc/rfc
- *load_library/1:* finds numbered sections, appendices and appendix subsections
- *load_library/1:* every RFC in the library has a section 1
- *validate/2:* accepts a reference to an existing section
- *validate/2:* rejects an RFC that is not in the library
- *validate/2:* rejects a section that does not exist
- *validate/2:* passes on parse errors

### `Mix.Lumina.TestScannerTest`

[test/mix/lumina/test_scanner_test.exs](../../test/mix/lumina/test_scanner_test.exs)

Tests the static test scanner that drives the RFC reference check, the
unit-test documentation check and the unit-test section of the catalog.
Sample test files are given as source strings and parsed, never compiled.

- *RFC references:* collects @tag, @describetag and @moduletag references, outermost first
- *RFC references:* @tag applies only to the next test
- *RFC references:* @describetag does not leak out of its describe block
- *RFC references:* reports tags whose value is not a literal string or list of strings
- *RFC references:* validate_refs/2 returns one problem per invalid reference, naming the test
- *modules and tests:* collects every test with its module, describe block and ExUnit name
- *modules and tests:* reads @moduledoc from a string, a heredoc, a ~S sigil, or false
- *modules and tests:* records whether a module uses ExUnit.Case
- *modules and tests:* names nested modules after their parent
- *modules and tests:* @tag doc: is attached to the next test only
- *modules and tests:* rejects doc: that is blank, not a literal, or not on @tag
- *modules and tests:* reports files that cannot be parsed
- *check_docs/1:* passes a documented module
- *check_docs/1:* fails a test module without @moduledoc
- *check_docs/1:* fails a test module with @moduledoc false
- *check_docs/1:* fails a blank @moduledoc
- *check_docs/1:* fails a blank test name
- *check_docs/1:* ignores helper modules that don't use ExUnit.Case

### `Mix.Tasks.Lumina.Asn1.ExtractTest`

[test/mix/tasks/lumina.asn1.extract_test.exs](../../test/mix/tasks/lumina.asn1.extract_test.exs)

Tests the extraction task, especially --check, which makes CI fail when an
extracted or built module is edited by hand instead of being regenerated
from the RFC text and the patches. Also checks that broken or stray
patches stop the task.

- writes every extracted and built module, then --check passes
- the output matches what is committed
- --check fails when an extracted module was edited by hand
- --check fails when a built module was edited by hand
- --check fails on a file for a module that is no longer listed
- writing removes files for modules that are no longer listed
- fails when a patch no longer applies to the extracted text
- fails when a patch makes a change its kind doesn't allow
- fails on a patch for a module that isn't listed

### `Mix.Tasks.Lumina.Fixtures.GenTest`

[test/mix/tasks/lumina.fixtures.gen_test.exs](../../test/mix/tasks/lumina.fixtures.gen_test.exs)

Tests fixture generation with the real Barry binary: output layout,
removal of stale files, the fixed validity period, and that regenerating
gives the same file list and check result. Tagged :barry, so it is
excluded unless Barry is installed; CI runs it in the barry job.

- generates the TAL and rsync tree, and the fixture passes its check
- regenerating gives the same files and the same check result
- removes output that the descriptor no longer produces
- uses the fixed validity period, so fixtures don't expire

### `Mix.Tasks.Lumina.RfcCoverageTest`

[test/mix/tasks/lumina.rfc_coverage_test.exs](../../test/mix/tasks/lumina.rfc_coverage_test.exs)

Tests the RFC coverage report: covered sections in document order, and
the full per-RFC view used as the RFC 8897 requirements checklist.

- lists covered sections per RFC, in document order
- with an RFC, lists every section and marks the uncovered ones
- says so when no test references an RFC

### `Mix.Tasks.Lumina.TestCatalogTest`

[test/mix/tasks/lumina.test_catalog_test.exs](../../test/mix/tasks/lumina.test_catalog_test.exs)

Tests the catalog task, especially --check, which is what makes CI fail
when a fixture or test changes without the catalog being regenerated.
Fixtures and test sources are written to temporary directories.

- writes the catalog, then --check passes
- --check fails when a fixture is added without regenerating
- --check fails when a fixture changes without regenerating
- --check fails when a unit test is added without regenerating
- --check fails when the catalog is missing
- fails when a fixture fails its metadata check
- fails when a test module has no @moduledoc

### `Lumina.RFCReferencesTest`

[test/rfc_references_test.exs](../../test/rfc_references_test.exs)

Enforces that every :rfc tag in the test suite points to an RFC and
section that exist in doc/rfc, so the coverage report and the catalog
never cite text we don't have. See doc/testing.md.

- every RFC reference in the test suite is valid

### `Lumina.TestDocsTest`

[test/test_docs_test.exs](../../test/test_docs_test.exs)

Enforces the rule that every unit test is documented (doc/testing.md):
every test module has a @moduledoc and every test a non-blank name. It
also checks that the static scanner behind the test catalog sees exactly
the tests ExUnit runs, so the catalog can't silently miss one.

- every test module has a @moduledoc and every test a name
- the scanner finds exactly the tests ExUnit runs, in every loaded test module
  When run with the whole suite, this covers every test module. When a
  single file is run, it covers the modules ExUnit loaded for that run.
  Doctests are excluded: they are documented by the function docs they
  come from.
